fields.TOPIC: Obligation to provide the European Digital Identity Wallet
fields.CONTENT: Each Member State (MS) shall provide AT LEAST ONE European Digital Identity Wallet. Purpose according to the wording: secure, trusted and seamless cross-border access to public AND private services, while having full control over their data.
fields.PURPOSE: Without an obligation to provide it, the European Digital Identity Wallet would remain a non-binding offer; only the obligation brings about the EU-wide rollout.
fields.DEADLINE: 24 months after the entry into force of the implementing acts under Article 5a(23) AND Article 5c(6) – the period does NOT run from the date of the Regulation
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 5a(23) · Implementing act on the core European Digital Identity Wallet requirements The Regulation's most important empowering provision in practice. The Commission establishes reference standards, specifications and procedures for paragraphs 4, 5, 8 and 18 – that is the legal basis of the Architecture and Reference Framework. It is at the same time one of the two triggers of the 24-month period under paragraph 1. Numerous further provisions (Article 5b(11), Article 5d(7), Article 5e(5), Article 45d(5), Article 45e(2), Article 45f(6) and (7)) expressly require alignment with that act. “the Commission shall, by means of implementing acts, establish a list of reference standards and, where necessary, establish specifications and procedures for the requirements referred to in paragraphs 4, 5, 8 and 18 of this Article” ✓ Article 5a(23) eIDAS Relevance here: Without that act, paragraphs 4, 5, 8 and 18 cannot be audited; it is also the anchor for the time limit under paragraph 1. Article 5c(6) · Implementing act on European Digital Identity Wallet certification Establishes reference standards, specifications and procedures for the certification under paragraphs 1, 2 and 3. Together with Article 5a(23), the second trigger of the 24-month period. Without a uniform certification scheme, a European Digital Identity Wallet certificate from one Member State would not be reliable in another – and the list under Article 5d would have no common yardstick. Relevance here: The second trigger of the same period – if either of the two acts is missing, the 24-month clock under paragraph 1 does not start to run at all. Article 5f(2) · Acceptance obligation of certain private entities Covers private relying parties which, under Union law, national law or by contract, are required to carry out strong user authentication – the areas named include transport, energy, banking, financial services, social security, health, digital infrastructure, education and telecommunications. Microenterprises and small enterprises are exempt; acceptance takes place only upon the voluntary request of the user. Time limit: 36 months from the same anchor as Article 5a(1). “Where private relying parties that provide services, with the exception of microenterprises and small enterprises” ✓ Article 5f(2) eIDAS Article 52 eIDAS · Entry into force Staggers the date of application: the general rule is 1 July 2016; the empowering provisions referred to in paragraph 2, point (a) already apply from 17 September 2014; Articles 7, 8(1) and (2), 9, 10, 11 and 12(1) apply from the date of application of the implementing acts under Article 8(3) and Article 12(8); and the recognition obligation under Article 6 takes effect only three years thereafter.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Is the European Digital Identity Wallet provided under an electronic identification (eID) scheme at assurance level high (paragraph 11)?
fields.KEY POINT: 'At least one' – a Member State (MS) may have several, but never zero.

fields.TOPIC: The three ways of providing the European Digital Identity Wallet
fields.CONTENT: Three permissible models: (a) directly by the Member State (MS), (b) under a mandate from the MS, (c) independently of the MS but recognised by it. No ranking, no preference.
fields.PURPOSE: Permits private European Digital Identity Wallet providers without giving up the responsibility of the State – in all three cases the Member State remains the guarantor.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 5a(14) · User control and logical separation Prohibits the European Digital Identity Wallet provider from collecting usage information that is not necessary and from combining European Digital Identity Wallet data with data from its own other services or from third-party services. The provider must in addition keep the data logically separate from all other holdings. Where provision is private under paragraph 2, point (b) or (c), Article 45h(3) (functional separation) applies in addition, mutatis mutandis. This is the only paragraph outside paragraphs 4, 5 and 8 that is expressly certified. “Personal data relating to the provision of the European Digital Identity Wallet shall be kept logically separate from any other data held by the provider of the European Digital Identity Wallet” ✓ Article 5a(14) eIDAS Article 45h(3) eIDAS · Functional separation Requires providers to deliver qualified electronic attestation of attributes services in such a way that they are functionally separate from their other services. Via Article 5a(14), that provision applies mutatis mutandis to private European Digital Identity Wallet providers as well. Relevance here: It applies only where provision is private under paragraph 2, point (b) or (c), and adds functional separation to logical separation. Article 4 eIDAS · Internal market principle Prohibits Member States from restricting the provision of trust services from another Member State for reasons falling within the scope of the Regulation. Paragraph 2 requires that products and services lawfully provided in one Member State be able to circulate freely in the internal market. The general rule is spelled out for qualified services in Article 24a. Article 46a eIDAS · Supervision of the European Digital Identity Wallet framework Requires Member States to designate supervisory bodies for European Digital Identity Wallet providers and to notify them to the Commission. Those bodies monitor compliance with the requirements, may require evidence and may order measures. Before eIDAS 2.0 there was no comparable supervisory structure for the electronic identification (eID) pillar.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Which model does the Member State (MS) use – and who is then the addressee of supervision under Article 46a?
fields.KEY POINT: State, mandate, recognition – three routes, one responsible party.

fields.TOPIC: Open-source obligation for the source code
fields.ADDRESSEE: European Digital Identity Wallet provider / Member State
fields.CONTENT: The source code of the APPLICATION SOFTWARE COMPONENTS shall be open-source licensed. Exception: for duly justified reasons a Member State (MS) may provide that the source code of specific components other than those installed on user devices is NOT disclosed (server side).
fields.PURPOSE: Verifiability instead of a leap of faith – the security of an identity application must be publicly auditable.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 5c · Certification of the European Digital Identity Wallet Provides that the European Digital Identity Wallet and the underlying electronic identification (eID) scheme are certified by designated conformity assessment bodies, and divides up the assessment: cybersecurity requirements via the schemes under the Cybersecurity Act, everything else via national certification schemes, the drafts of which are to be submitted to the Cooperation Group. In addition, it governs the five-year limit with a two-yearly vulnerability assessment, the optional certification under the GDPR, the implementing act and a delegated act on the criteria for the assessment bodies.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Is the client source code in fact published under an open-source licence? Is every exception documented and justified?
fields.KEY POINT: Client open, server may stay closed – but only with justification.

fields.ADDRESSEE: European Digital Identity Wallet (technical) / European Digital Identity Wallet provider
fields.CONTENT: The European Digital Identity Wallet SHALL enable the user to perform functions (a) to (g) in a manner that is user-friendly, transparent and traceable by the user. Points (a) to (g) are CUMULATIVE.
fields.PURPOSE: A European Digital Identity Wallet that is secure but unusable will not be used – here usability is a legal obligation, not an optional extra.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 5a(23) · Implementing act on the core European Digital Identity Wallet requirements The Regulation's most important empowering provision in practice. The Commission establishes reference standards, specifications and procedures for paragraphs 4, 5, 8 and 18 – that is the legal basis of the Architecture and Reference Framework. It is at the same time one of the two triggers of the 24-month period under paragraph 1. Numerous further provisions (Article 5b(11), Article 5d(7), Article 5e(5), Article 45d(5), Article 45e(2), Article 45f(6) and (7)) expressly require alignment with that act. “the Commission shall, by means of implementing acts, establish a list of reference standards and, where necessary, establish specifications and procedures for the requirements referred to in paragraphs 4, 5, 8 and 18 of this Article” ✓ Article 5a(23) eIDAS Relevance here: Without that act, paragraphs 4, 5, 8 and 18 cannot be audited; it is also the anchor for the time limit under paragraph 1.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Are all seven functions (a) to (g) present – or is one missing?
fields.KEY POINT: Paragraph 4 = what the USER can do. Paragraph 5 = what the TECHNOLOGY must be able to do.

fields.CONTENT: Securely requesting, obtaining, selecting, combining, storing, deleting, sharing and presenting electronic attestations of attributes (EAA) and person identification data – under the SOLE control of the user, online and, where appropriate, in offline mode. Selective disclosure SHALL be possible.
fields.PURPOSE: Data minimisation put into practice: proof of age without a date of birth, proof of residence without a street address.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 5b(3) · Prohibition of over-asking Makes the registration information under paragraph 2, point (c) legally binding: the registered scope of data is at the same time the maximum permissible scope. Purpose limitation under data protection law thereby becomes enforceable technically and by supervision for the first time, instead of merely being asserted. “shall not request users to provide any data other than that indicated pursuant to paragraph 2, point (c)” ✓ Article 5b(3) eIDAS Article 45g eIDAS · Issuance of electronic attestations of attributes to Wallets Paragraph 1 requires ALL providers of electronic attestations of attributes to enable European Digital Identity Wallet users to request, obtain, store and manage them irrespective of the Member State of provision. Paragraph 2 requires in addition – but only of providers of QUALIFIED electronic attestations of attributes – an interface to the European Digital Identity Wallet. Without that bridge the European Digital Identity Wallet would remain empty.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Can the user selectively disclose individual attributes – or only the entire data record?
fields.KEY POINT: Selective disclosure is the core: prove age without disclosing the date of birth.

fields.CONTENT: Generating pseudonyms and storing them ENCRYPTED and LOCALLY within the European Digital Identity Wallet.
fields.PURPOSE: Pseudonyms are effective in data protection terms only if they are not held by the provider – local + encrypted is the condition.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 5b(9) · Responsibility for validation and protection of pseudonyms Places responsibility for the authentication and validation of the data presented on the relying party – not on the European Digital Identity Wallet provider. The second sentence also prohibits refusing the use of pseudonyms unless a legal provision requires identification by real name. Article 5 is thereby protected against being circumvented in practice. Article 5 eIDAS · Use of pseudonyms A single, unnumbered sentence: without prejudice to specific identification obligations and to the legal effect of pseudonyms under national law, the use of pseudonyms chosen by the user shall not be prohibited in electronic transactions. The Article has NO paragraphs. It is given specific effect in Article 5a(4), point (b), Article 5b(9) and Article 32(1), point (e). Article 2 eIDAS · Scope Covers notified electronic identification (eID) schemes, the Wallets provided by the Member States and trust service providers established in the Union. Expressly NOT covered are trust services provided, under national law or under an agreement, exclusively within a closed group of participants – enterprise-internal PKI therefore falls outside. Paragraph 3 makes clear that the Regulation does not affect national contract law or the GDPR.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Are pseudonyms stored locally on the device and in encrypted form?
fields.KEY POINT: Pseudonym = local + encrypted. Held server-side, it would not be one.

fields.TOPIC: European Digital Identity Wallet-to-European Digital Identity Wallet interaction
fields.CONTENT: Securely authenticating ANOTHER person's European Digital Identity Wallet and receiving and sharing person identification data (PID) and electronic attestations of attributes (EAA) between two Wallets.
fields.PURPOSE: Person-to-person attestations (tenancy agreement, contract of sale, power of attorney) without a detour via a service provider.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 5a(5) · Mandatory technical characteristics The inside view of paragraph 4. Point (a) lists eleven interfaces (issuance, request, presentation, user interaction, onboarding, European Digital Identity Wallet-to-European Digital Identity Wallet, relying party (RP) authentication, verification of authenticity, erasure requests, reporting to authorities, creation of qualified electronic signatures) – in effect the table of contents of the ARF. Point (b) prohibits any feedback to the issuer of the electronic attestation of attributes (EAA), point (d) mandates assurance level high (LoA high) and point (g) the free-of-charge qualified electronic signature for natural persons.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Is person-to-person (P2P) interaction implemented, or only the classic user-to-relying-party flow?
fields.KEY POINT: The Wallet is not only an identity document, but also a counterparty.

fields.CONTENT: Access to a log of ALL transactions via a common dashboard, so that the user can (i) view all relying parties (RP) and the data shared, (ii) easily request erasure pursuant to Article 17 GDPR, (iii) easily report unlawful or suspicious requests for data to the national data protection authority.
fields.PURPOSE: Without a transparency tool the user cannot exercise the 'sole control' under paragraph 4, point (a) at all.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 17 GDPR · Right to erasure – right to be forgotten Paragraph 1 gives the data subject the right to obtain erasure without undue delay, inter alia where the data are no longer necessary for the purposes of the processing, where consent has been withdrawn, where an objection has been lodged or where the processing was unlawful. Paragraph 2 requires other controllers to be informed where the data have been made public. Paragraph 3 sets out exceptions, for example for legal obligations and for the establishment or exercise of legal claims. Link to eIDAS: Article 5a(4), point (d)(ii) eIDAS requires the user to be able to make that erasure request EASILY, directly from the European Digital Identity Wallet dashboard – the right is thus translated into an operating function. ● Summary of content, not verified against the original text Article 5a(5) · Mandatory technical characteristics The inside view of paragraph 4. Point (a) lists eleven interfaces (issuance, request, presentation, user interaction, onboarding, European Digital Identity Wallet-to-European Digital Identity Wallet, relying party (RP) authentication, verification of authenticity, erasure requests, reporting to authorities, creation of qualified electronic signatures) – in effect the table of contents of the ARF. Point (b) prohibits any feedback to the issuer of the electronic attestation of attributes (EAA), point (d) mandates assurance level high (LoA high) and point (g) the free-of-charge qualified electronic signature for natural persons.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Does the dashboard contain all three functions (viewing, erasure request, reporting) – or only the history?
fields.KEY POINT: Dashboard = view, erase, report. Three buttons, not one.

fields.TOPIC: Signing and sealing from the European Digital Identity Wallet
fields.CONTENT: Signing by means of qualified electronic signatures or sealing by means of qualified electronic seals.
fields.PURPOSE: Connects the electronic identification (eID) pillar (Chapter II) directly with the trust services pillar (Chapter III) – the European Digital Identity Wallet becomes a signature application.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 5a(5) · Mandatory technical characteristics The inside view of paragraph 4. Point (a) lists eleven interfaces (issuance, request, presentation, user interaction, onboarding, European Digital Identity Wallet-to-European Digital Identity Wallet, relying party (RP) authentication, verification of authenticity, erasure requests, reporting to authorities, creation of qualified electronic signatures) – in effect the table of contents of the ARF. Point (b) prohibits any feedback to the issuer of the electronic attestation of attributes (EAA), point (d) mandates assurance level high (LoA high) and point (g) the free-of-charge qualified electronic signature for natural persons. Article 25 eIDAS · Legal effects of electronic signatures Contains two sentences of far-reaching significance: paragraph 1 prohibits denying an electronic signature legal effect and admissibility as evidence solely on the ground that it is in electronic form or that it does not meet the requirements for qualified electronic signatures. Paragraph 2 gives the qualified electronic signature the equivalent legal effect of a handwritten signature. The former paragraph 3 was deleted by eIDAS 2.0. Article 29a eIDAS · Qualified service for the management of remote electronic signature creation devices Makes the server-side management of signature keys a qualified trust service in its own right, subject to three conditions: generation or management of the electronic signature creation data on behalf of the signatory; duplication of that data solely for back-up purposes, at the same level of security and in no more copies than strictly necessary; and compliance with all requirements set out in the certification report under Article 30. Grandfathering applies until 21 May 2026.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Is the qualified electronic signature created by means of a certified qualified electronic signature creation device (QSCD) or by a qualified trust service provider (QTSP) under Article 29a?
fields.KEY POINT: The Wallet is the bridge between Chapter II and Chapter III.
